seasons.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), May-June 2021 (CSIR-CIMAP): Livelihood security of small and marginal farmers through Ocimum cultivation

expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.title: TNAU Agritech Portal, medicinal crops
expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.quote: On an average, tulsi gives about 10,000 kgs of fresh herbage per hectare per year.
expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.note: 10 t/ha = 1.0 kg/m² of fresh herbage per year (lowest figure; CIMAP gives 20 t/ha).

economics.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), May-June 2021 (CSIR-CIMAP): Livelihood security of small and marginal farmers through Ocimum cultivation
economics.quote: Tulsi farming involves an average cost of cultivation ` 45,000/ ha and gross returns of ` 1,00,000/ha after selling the herb, thus leading to a net return of ` 55,000/ha.
economics.note: CSIR-CIMAP estimate for oil and herb sold; the buyer has to be found first.

economics.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), May-June 2021 (CSIR-CIMAP): Livelihood security of small and marginal farmers through Ocimum cultivation
economics.quote: in rainfed areas in Kharif season as it requires lower input and gives better returns

source_notes: AI research batch 15 (2026-10-08), medicinal and ayurvedic crops. Ranges are stored at their lower bound; the source range is in each quote. Yields are of the dried product that is sold (dried root, leaf or seed) unless a note says fresh. Sowing dates are from national guides (region india) unless a Malwa study is named. Medicinal crops are planned only when the owner picks the medicinal method; the market for each is thin and buy-back is not assured (see the economics sources).
